title: A Face Only a Mother Could Love
synopsis: A lonely Parisian dancer with an unusual appearance longs for connection, until an unexpected encounter opens up the possibility of love.

paragraphs: From the very first moments, you become completely immersed in the French atmosphere. The visuals of Paris inevitably bring Amélie to mind, while the French accent adds a distinctive charm to the storytelling — something rarely found in most AI-generated films.

In just eight minutes, Robert Gaudette draws us into a captivating story that's almost impossible to look away from. It's reminiscent of other unforgettable tales about extraordinary outsiders and their unconventional lives. Tim Burton's Edward Scissorhands, starring Johnny Depp, comes to mind, as does Guillermo del Toro's Oscar-winning The Shape of Water.
editorialReview.verdict: If you want to see what an Oscar-worthy AI film could look like, A Face Only a Mother Could Love is an absolute must-watch.

audienceReactions.quote: Wild this only has a thousand views. Well done.

audienceReactions.quote: This is great European cinema, enriched by that exciting new element — AI. I hope that one day, when people look back and discuss the history of AI cinema, your film will be remembered as one of its important building blocks — or perhaps even as one of its foundational stones. Congratulations!
